    AI Overview
    The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday evening, April 10, 2026. The splashdown is expected around 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT), concluding a 10-day mission around the moon approximately 40-50 miles off the coast. 
    Key Details for the Splashdown: 
    • Location: Pacific Ocean, roughly 40-50 miles off the San Diego coast.
    • Date/Time: Friday, April 10, 2026, around 8:07 p.m. ET / 5:07 p.m. PT.
    • Recovery Team: NASA and U.S. Navy teams on the USS John P. Murtha.
    • Crew: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen. 
    The capsule will re-enter the atmosphere at high speed before deploying parachutes to slow down to about 17-20 mph for the final water landing. Residents in Southern California might hear a sonic boom associated with the re-entry.
